title: Econ heuristic compiler and traffic-shaping profile generator
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers with mixed latency/throughput workloads needed a lightweight offline compiler to synthesize safe candidate profiles (batching, prefix caching, quantization hints, and traffic-shaping weightings) that can be validated via simulation before canary rollout. This PR introduces an econ heuristic compiler and a traffic-shaping profile generator plus CLI tooling to produce, evaluate, and export profile bundles for Redwood Optimize workflows. Changes include a new package for heuristic compilation, integration hooks for the Optimize API, a redwoodctl subcommand to run offline sims, a staging canary rollout plan, and operator docs. Checklist: 1) Implement heuristic compiler and traffic-shaper; 2) Add CLI commands and examples; 3) Add unit and simulation tests; 4) Add docs and operator notes; 5) Run staging canary and monitor regressions; 6) Address reviewer feedback; 7) Squash-merge. Impact: Non-breaking, opt-in tooling for profile generation and safe rollouts; default behavior unchanged until profiles are explicitly applied. Rollout plan: land in main behind feature-flag, run staged canaries on two internal tenants for 48 hours, then enable broader rollout. Related: ENG-CLK-1421 for compiler heuristics, ENG-BI-2113 for traffic-shaping metrics ingestion. Usage: `redwoodctl econ compile --workload sample.yaml --out bundle.tgz` produces a bundle with candidate batch/cache/quant profiles and a small simulation report. Migration notes: none required for existing configs, operators may optionally adopt exported bundles or wire Optimize to apply them automatically.

release_notes: Adds an offline econ heuristic compiler that synthesizes candidate batching/caching/quantization profiles and a traffic-shaping profile generator; introduces `redwoodctl econ compile` to emit bundles and a simulation report; safe canary rollout plan and operator docs included; opt-in only, non-breaking.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover heuristic pipeline and traffic-shaper logic. Simulation harness ran across four workload shapes (interactive, bursty, streaming, conversational) with 10k simulated requests each. Median cost reduction across sample workloads: 12%. P95 latency impact: +2.7% median, within SLO for canary. Staging canary on two tenants for 48 hours with monitor dashboards passed; one quant suggestion path was disabled and fixed during canary. Manual verification steps and replay scripts added to docs.
motivation_context: This PR reduces operator effort and risk when adopting automated econ profiles by letting teams compile candidate profiles offline, validate them via deterministic simulation, and then rollout under a canary with automatic fallback. It closes gaps identified in ENG-CLK-1421 and helps Optimize accept higher-confidence profile proposals.
